name: Allium
look_here_first: Confirm onion odor, bulb, spathe-bracted umbel and six tepals. Inspect flowers versus aerial bulbils and the veins of an intact papery spathe.
shared_traits: Bulbous herbs with onion odor, basal linear leaves, a leafless scape and umbel.
Six tepals, six stamens and superior ovary; capsules develop from flowers.

comparison.canadense: Aerial bulbils often present, sometimes replacing flowers
comparison.drummondii: Usually many flowers; bulbils not an absolute exclusion

comparison.canadense: Detailed local var. canadense treatment reports numerous veins
comparison.drummondii: Detailed Williamson County treatment reports 3–4 veins and 3 tail-like tips
Flowers approximately 10–12 mm across in local description

cautions: Flower color and bulbil presence alone do not decide the species.
Variety-level measurements for A. canadense should not be universalized.

lookalikes.name: Zephyranthes
lookalikes.difference: Inferior ovary, often solitary larger flower

photo_targets: Whole umbel with flowers and bulbils
Flower face and side with scale

handoffs.need: Reconcile both source-pool taxa with canonical manifest; no species installation in this lesson.
Matched reproductive macro views for both species.
